Boundary Surface's Fill a Loop through guide curves (mitcad#2526, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#711) on the reported design (opened with --open, never committed; tools/cli/boundary-guides-reported-test.cmake): sketches and construction planes only, no bodies. Sketch3 (F4) lies on Plane1 (F3), the plane Z = -38.904 through Sketch2's construction line c34, and holds the bowl's rim projected from Sketch1's outline: seven arcs c1, c5, c9, c13, c17, c21, c25 closing one loop from the tip at (0, 0) to the neck at (64.8, 0), at most 22.032 mm off the X axis (c1 and c17, radius 50), its region 2215.268 mm2 (by the arcs). The depth curves inside it: Sketch2's (F2, on XZ, its y along +Z) arcs c39 (radius d10 = 110 mm) from the tip down to (43.2, 0, -47.501) and c36 from there up to the neck, the lowest point of both (42.634, 0, -47.502); Sketch4's (F6, on Plane2, X = 43.2) arc c4 across the bowl from rim to rim through c39's end; Sketch5's (F8, on Plane3, X = 21.6) arc c4 across it through c39 at Z = -45.472. Their ends lie on the rim; Sketch4's and Sketch5's points are sections of Sketch2's c39 and the rim, so they follow an edit of Sketch2.
The rim without guides, its seven arcs picked as single curves: the flat region the rim bounds, as a planar loop fills without guides.

The same rim through the four depth curves as guides, as Boundary Surface's panel sends it (one entry for each sketch): the preview, then the feature, which commits what the preview computed. One valid face whose edges are the rim's seven arcs alone (no guide bounds or splits it); the feature is refused unless the face lies within 0.01 mm of every guide and of the rim (geometry/src/surface_fills.cpp, check_guided), so its status ok says it runs through them. The face spans the rim and hangs from it down to the guides' lowest point, Z -47.502 (within the 0.01 mm, and a little below it between the guides).
The guides stay references of the feature, as editing it restores them.

An edit of a guide's sketch: Sketch2's d10 (c39's radius) 110 -> 100 mm. c39 still runs from the tip to X = 43.2, tangent there to c36, which meets the neck tangent to the handle's arc c31 (unchanged); solved, c39 ends at Z -47.704 and its lowest point is (41.068, 0, -47.726), c36's radius 32.625. Sketch4's and Sketch5's sections of c39 move with it, their arcs through them. The face is made again through the deeper guides; the rim and its flat fill stay as they were.
Back to 110 mm: the face computed again, not from the preview, is the one the preview made.
A guide outside the rim, Sketch2's handle arc c31 from the neck up to (75.6, 0, -32.904): no face of the loop runs through it, refused in words.
